title: डॉक्टर के पास — at the doctor
summary: Pain, fever and what has already been taken. The dative-subject construction Hindi uses for how you feel.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: मेरे पेट में बहुत दर्द है।
lines.reading: Mere peṭ mein bahut dard hai.
lines.translation: I have a lot of pain in my stomach.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: हाँ, कल रात एक सौ एक था।
lines.reading: Hān, kal rāt ek sau ek thā.
lines.translation: Yes, last night it was a hundred and one.

lines.speaker: B
lines.translation: Yes, but it gave no relief.

lines.speaker: A
lines.translation: Are you allergic to any medicine?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: ज़्यादा पानी पीजिए और आराम कीजिए।
lines.reading: Zyādā pānī pījiye aur ārām kījiye.
lines.translation: Drink plenty of water and rest.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: कल भी दर्द हो तो फिर आइए।
lines.reading: Kal bhī dard ho to phir āiye.
lines.translation: If it still hurts tomorrow, come again.

vocabulary.meaning: pain — Hindi says 'to me there is pain', not 'I hurt'
since, for (a length of time) — tīn din se, for three days
fever — usually given in Fahrenheit in India

questions.explain: ek sau ek — India usually gives body temperature in Fahrenheit, so 101 °F is about 38.3 °C.

questions.q: What should he do if it still hurts tomorrow?
